derivations.quote: Every such $A$ factors as $A=E_1\Pi E_2$, where $E_1,E_2$ are invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ has exactly $a$ ones, at most one per row and column

Take the topmost nonzero row and its rightmost nonzero entry, the pivot. Right multiplication by lower triangular elementary matrices clears the row to the left of the pivot, and left multiplication by such matrices clears the column below it; scaling makes the pivot one. Delete the pivot row and column and repeat.
For $A$ in a fixed finite set, it can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields and $O(V)$ further work

Hence choose $q$ to avoid every denominator in the table and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor, so that the identities specialise to $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ and the triangular factors remain invertible.

Update coordinates in descending physical order. Coordinate $i$ becomes its diagonal unit times itself plus a fixed combination of earlier coordinates, which still hold their original values. With $m$ fixed, this costs $O(V)$.
Transform $D$ by $E_2$ and $H$ by $E_1^{-1}$, add $\Pi D$ to $H$, then transform $H$ by $E_1$ and $D$ by $E_2^{-1}$.
Do it by $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, then interchange $(H_i,D_j)$, then $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$. The first and last updates target a later field controlled by an earlier one, so they are controlled shifts.

This uses one interchange per one of $\Pi$, and $\Pi$ has $a$ ones, so exactly $a$ interchanges are used. Everything else lies within the $O(V)$ further work, so temporary tapes do not multiply the count.

relations.quote: Each lower triangular transformation of $H$ or of $D$ is carried out by [Controlled shifts and rational scalings](controlled-shifts.md).

symbols.name: field base
symbols.meaning: A fixed odd prime, the base of the digits.
symbols.quote: Here $q$ is a fixed odd prime, the base of the digits, not a sequence length.

symbols.name: digits per field
symbols.meaning: The number of base-q digits in one field.
symbols.quote: Here $b$ is the number of base-$q$ digits in one field, not the lowest bit of an index.

symbols.name: rank
symbols.meaning: The rank of the matrix A.
symbols.quote: Here $a$ is the rank of $A$, not an offset added to a field.

symbols.name: fields per group
symbols.meaning: The number of fields in each of the groups H and D.
symbols.quote: Let $H=(H_1,\dots,H_m)$ and $D=(D_1,\dots,D_m)$ be two groups of fields, $H$ before $D$, where $m$ is the number of fields in each group ($m$ counts fields here; it is not an output index).
